title: Sum Object Values
description: Given an object where all values are numbers, return the sum of all values.
whatShouldHappen: Use Object.values() to get an array of the values.
Loop through the values and add each to the total.
patternExplanation: Object.values() converts an object's values into a plain array — you can then use any array loop pattern on them without needing for...in.

title: Invert an Object
description: Given an object, return a new object where the keys and values are swapped. Assume all values are unique strings or numbers.
whatShouldHappen: Use Object.entries() to get [key, value] pairs.
For each pair, assign result[value] = key.
patternExplanation: Object.entries() yields [key, value] tuples — destructuring them in the loop header makes swapping or transforming key-value pairs clean and direct.

title: Deep Equal Comparison
description: Write a function that deeply compares two objects or values for equality, checking all keys and nested structures recursively.
whatShouldHappen: If values are strictly identical (===), return true.
If either is null, or not an object, return false.
Check array matching: if Array.isArray differs, return false.
Recursively compare every key's corresponding value.
patternExplanation: Traversing keys recursively handles nested object hierarchies while properly short-circuiting on primitive mismatches.

title: Invert Object Keys and Values
description: Given an object, return a new object where keys become values and values become keys. If multiple keys have the same value, group the original keys into an array.
whatShouldHappen: Loop through each key in the input object using for...in with hasOwnProperty.
Convert value to string for inverted key.
If the new key already exists, convert to or push into an array.
Otherwise, assign the single key as value.
patternExplanation: Flipping keys and values tests dynamic key access and handling collisions through conditional array accumulation.

title: Pick Object Properties
description: Given an object and an array of string keys, return a new object containing only the properties whose keys appear in the provided keys array.
whatShouldHappen: Create a Set from the keys array for fast O(1) checks.
Iterate over keys in Set: if obj has property, copy it to picked.
patternExplanation: Filtering object properties based on a whitelist is a core utility pattern in data sanitization and state manipulation.

title: Count Frequency of Elements
description: Given an array of string items, return an object mapping each unique item to its count of occurrences in the array.
whatShouldHappen: Loop through each item in the items array.
patternExplanation: Using an object as a hash map to aggregate item counts in a single O(n) pass is the basis of countless frequency patterns.

title: Scale Object Numeric Values
description: Given an object obj whose values are numbers and a numeric factor, return a new object where each property value is multiplied by factor using Object.entries().
whatShouldHappen: Iterate through [key, value] pairs of Object.entries(obj).
Multiply value by factor and assign to result[key].
patternExplanation: Object.entries() produces an array of [key, value] tuples, enabling clean destructuring in for...of loops for transforming object properties.

title: Filter Object by Property Value Threshold
description: Given an object obj whose values are numbers, and a number minThreshold, return a new object containing only properties whose values are greater than or equal to minThreshold.
whatShouldHappen: Initialize a new empty result object.
Iterate through entries of obj with Object.entries(obj).
If value >= minThreshold, assign result[key] = value.
patternExplanation: Iterating entries and conditionally setting properties on a fresh object creates an immutable filtered copy.

title: Count Property Types in Object
description: Given an object obj, iterate over its values using Object.values(obj) and return an object counting occurrences of each typeof primitive (e.g. 'string', 'number', 'boolean').
patternExplanation: Object.values() extracts property values directly, simplifying tallying and histogram creation when keys are not needed.

title: Format Object to Query String Pairs
description: Given an object params representing query parameters, iterate over Object.entries(params) and return an array of strings in 'key=value' format. If params is empty, return [].
whatShouldHappen: Format string using template literal `${key}=${value}` and push to pairs.
patternExplanation: Transforming entries into formatted strings using template literals is the fundamental step for URL query strings, HTTP headers, and configuration files.

title: Merge and Sum Object Counts
description: Given two objects objA and objB whose values are numeric quantities, return a merged object where each key value is the sum of its counts from both objects. Use for...in or Object.keys() to visit all keys.
whatShouldHappen: Initialize a result object with a shallow clone of objA.
Loop through keys of objB using Object.keys(objB).
patternExplanation: Cloning the initial object and aggregating secondary entries using logical OR fallback (result[key] || 0) cleanly sums inventory counts.
